description: Adversaries may take control of preexisting sessions with remote services to move laterally in an environment. User authentication to remote services will often generate a remote session with a temporary credential for continued access. An adversary may take advantage of this to move laterally if they have compromised a user's account or can intercept an existing session. Common session hijacking targets include SSH, RDP, and VNC sessions.

falco.trigger_condition: Unexpected SSH session takeover via UNIX domain socket injection (e.g. /proc/<pid>/fd/ manipulation to hijack an SSH agent). Falco can detect unusual reads of /proc filesystem entries associated with running SSH agents.

mitigation: Disable SSH agent forwarding unless strictly necessary. Use separate accounts and credentials for each administrative session. Monitor for unexpected access to /proc/*/fd/ paths. Implement session inactivity timeouts.
